fluff.overview: Mobile Army Surgical Hospitals have served as the backbone of battlefield medicine since their earliest predecessors on ancient Terra. The modern MASH truck concept emerged during the Age of War, when purpose-built mobile surgical platforms dramatically improved wounded soldiers' survival rates by as much as three hundred percent. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere produce MASH trucks in various configurations, making them one of the most ubiquitous support vehicles in military service. The representative model documented here is the twenty-ton Talon Vehicles "Mercy" pattern from the Federated Suns, first introduced in 2671. Carrying five fully equipped operating theaters on a wheeled chassis, the Mercy set a standard that many subsequent designs sought to match. MASH trucks occupy a unique position on the battlefield, broadly respected as non-combatants by all parties due to their tradition of treating wounded regardless of allegiance.
fluff.capabilities:
The Talon Vehicles MASH truck carries seven and a half tons of advanced medical equipment distributed across five folding operating theaters. When deployed, each theater extends from the main vehicle to create a temporary surgical structure equipped with an automated surgery table. Multiple robotic arms prep patients and assist the surgeon during operations. Each table can convert into an airtight cryo-tube, filling with clear oxygenated liquid to stabilize critical patients while allowing continued surgery through attached sleeves. An onboard medical computer suggests treatment plans, provides real-time monitoring including X-ray capability, and stores post-operative data for satellite uplink to field hospitals and DropShips.

A VOX 80 fusion engine provides unlimited operational range and reliable power for sensitive medical systems. Four tons of StarSlab/Sheet armor offers reasonable protection against stray fire, though MASH trucks are rarely targeted deliberately. When packed for transit, the truck carries essential supplies, six patients, and one active theater, with limited surgery possible at speed. Redeployment takes less than four hours. Two ChisComp 32 small lasers serve only to deter theft. Many doctors have these weapons removed entirely, viewing armed medical vehicles as a violation of their Hippocratic oath.
fluff.deployment: The ICE variant emerged during the Succession Wars as fusion engine supplies dwindled across the Inner Sphere. Rather than leave damaged or engine-stripped MASH trucks idle, field technicians replaced their fusion plants with readily available internal combustion engines. This conversion proved deeply unpopular with medical staff, as the ICE power plant reduced available energy for surgical equipment and limited operational range. The power requirements for full medical operations proved too demanding for internal combustion alone, with surgeons reporting system outages during critical procedures. No purely ICE-equipped MASH trucks have been manufactured since 2815, but existing units remain in service wherever fusion replacements cannot be sourced.
fluff.history:
Talon Vehicles introduced the Mercy-pattern MASH truck in 2671, and the design quickly became the benchmark for mobile surgical platforms across the Inner Sphere. The concept spawned numerous regional variants adapted to each Great House's military culture. The Free Worlds League fielded "White Whale" convoys with seven-theater configurations, though soldiers dreaded seeing the yellow-cross markings of MediQuick Services and their notoriously poor quality of care. The Capellan Confederation's three-theater "Entitled" model was staffed by members of the dedicated medical caste and earned high regard from its patients. The Draconis Combine's five-theater "Health and Happiness" units drew the bitter nickname "Welcome Wagons," a grim reference to the Combine's "Welcoming Homes" hospice facilities. The Lyran Commonwealth produced the six-theater "Martin Luther" model, perhaps the most advanced MASH truck of the Succession Wars. Dark rumors persisted of modified "Claudius" variants used as mobile interrogation platforms by the Lyran Intelligence Corps.

The Succession Wars devastated fusion engine production, forcing many MASH operators to replace their VOX power plants with internal combustion engines. These ICE conversions reduced speed and available power for medical systems, diminishing overall capability. Though no new ICE-equipped MASH trucks have been manufactured since 2815, many remained in service out of sheer necessity throughout the late Succession Wars era.

MASH units have traditionally been considered inviolate on the battlefield. Even Clan warriors, who brought their own equivalent medical platforms during the invasion of the Inner Sphere, consider attacking a MASH to be a grave breach of honor. Warriors found guilty of deliberately targeting medical vehicles face expulsion from the warrior caste. This near-universal protection has made MASH units a rare point of common ground between otherwise implacable enemies, with wounded from both sides often receiving care under the same roof. Terran military historians often cite the legendary 4077th Surgical Company as the origin of this tradition, a unit renowned as much for its gallows humor as for providing what its staff called "the best care anywhere."
